newsitem.title: ZAIRE: French envoy calls for calm after two killed.
newsitem.headline: French envoy calls for calm after two killed.

text.p: The French ambassador in the Democratic Republic of Congo told his compatriots on Wednesday not to panic, saying there was no evidence two Frenchmen were killed by victorious Alliance troops in former Zaire.
Michel Rougagnou issued a statement seeking to calm fears in the 150-strong community in Kinshasa that the new authorities were virulently anti-French.
Businessmen Michel Tournaire and Herve Rigaud were shot dead on Tuesday evening in a plastics factory in the capital's Limete quarter.
"There is no reason to think that our compatriots were killed because they were French.
"Nor is there any reason to think the murders were perpetrated by the military units installing themselves gradually in the capital," Rougagnou said.
Rougagnou asked French residents to follow security guidelines closely "without giving in to panic".

France was a close ally of president Mobutu Sese Seko, who fled to Togo last weekend as Laurent Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL) marched into the capital after a seven-month rebellion.
The Alliance makes no secret of its dislike for France's post-colonial policy in Africa and anti-French sentiment is pronounced on the streets of Kinshasa.
Students marched in protest on the French embassy on Monday and angry residents frequently want to know if foreign journalists are French.

The French community in Kinshasa before the nervous build-up to the Alliance's arrival numbered 1,500, an embassy official said. A small minority remained, to protect their assets, after sending their families abroad.
The two Frenchmen's killers are unknown but Rougagnou said the Alliance, which issued a statement late on Tuesday deploring the murders, had opened an inquiry.
"We can only be encouraged by the spirit of cooperation which the Alliance's leaders have shown," he said.
Diplomatic sources, quoting witnesses, said four armed men, two in military uniform, arrived by car at the plastics factory. Two of the men ordered the Frenchmen into an office and shot them dead.
"There was no discussion and apparently nothing was stolen. The witnesses say they cannot tell if the killers were ex-Mobutu soldiers or Alliance fighters," one diplomat said.
Men of Mobutu's army and presidential guard, trapped in Kinshasa as others fled west or turned themselves in, are blamed for attacks, hold-ups and looting raids in the city since Saturday.
But there was concern in Western embassies that Alliance troops might also be involved in criminality.

Kabila's core fighters have a reputation for strong discipline but diplomats did not rule out that the wide coalition of foreign African and Zairean fighters which captured Kinshasa includes some uncontrolled units.
